title: Quasi-coherent modules detect Tor amplitude on affine schemes
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category], and let $a\le b$ be integers. Suppose $H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every integer $i<a$ or $b<i$, with vanishing as in [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. Then the same vanishing holds for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$, without a quasi-coherence hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, affine paragraph using Tag 06Z0 and Tag 08E9; Tag 08E9 proof using the bounded flat-model criterion of Tag 0654

proof.text: Use the existing affine module-complex representative theorem to obtain M with E isomorphic to Q(C(M)), where C is tilde followed by exact restriction along the canonical spectrum chart. Tilde is fully faithful and a left adjoint. Reuse tilde_preservesKernel from AffineDerivedTildeHomologyComparison through a proof-only import all; this existing proof lifts the quasi-coherent kernel fork through full faithfulness. Hence C is exact. Restriction along the chart has a left inverse by restriction-composition and the isomorphism identities, so C is faithful.

Resolve M by a module K-flat complex P. For every module N, C(N) is quasi-coherent. Apply the hypothesis to C(N). Reuse tensor_vanishes_iff from TorAmplitudeOpenLocal through a proof-only import all to identify this vanishing with zero homology of the derived tensor. The single-complex comparison and the affine derived tensor chart comparison identify this tensor with Q(C(Tot(P tensor N[0]))). Exactness of C identifies its homology with C of the module homology. Faithfulness reflects zero identity maps, hence the module homology vanishes. The K-flat module tensor model and the IsGE/IsLE cohomology criteria establish module Tor amplitude [a,b].

Apply the bounded flat-model criterion to M, obtaining a flat complex B with zero terms outside [a,b] and an isomorphism Q(M) to Q(B). Exactness of C transports this isomorphism to a representing isomorphism Q(C(B)) to E. B is K-flat because it is bounded above and flat; tilde and open restriction preserve K-flatness, so C(B) is a sheaf K-flat representative.

For any sheaf G, the total tensor C(B) tensor G[0] is isomorphic to the termwise tensor-right complex. Its degree i term is zero whenever i is outside [a,b], since additive C and tensor-right preserve zero objects. Zero degree-i term implies exactness at i and zero homology. C(B), its K-flatness, and the representing isomorphism give the required vanishing witness.

lean.statement:
theorem affineQCoh_torAmplitude_detection (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X E)
    (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (h : ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace),
      F.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i →
        schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes X E F i) :
    ∀ G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace),
      ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes X E G i
